question.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[X].$

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{6x}{5}, & 0<x<1 \\ \frac{2}{5x}, & 1\le x<e\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

$$
\text{E}[X]={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x
$$

 

We compute the expected value of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{0}^{e}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{e}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot \frac{6x}{5}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{e}x\cdot \frac{2}{5x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{6{x}^{2}}{5}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{2}{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{2{x}^{3}}{5}|}_{0}^{1}+{\frac{2x}{5}|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}+\frac{2e}{5}-\frac{2}{5} \\  & =\frac{2e}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
